title: Lower Body & Core Strength - Engelbrektsloppet Preparation

items.name: Cat-Cow
items.cues: Move slowly and deliberately, sync movement with breath. Arch and round the spine with control.

items.name: Bird Dog
items.cues: Extend opposite arm and leg simultaneously, maintain neutral spine. Pause 1 second at full extension.

items.name: 90/90 Hip Switches
items.cues: Keep chest upright, rotate from hips. Feel the stretch in external rotators and glutes.

items.name: Back Squat
items.cues: Drive through heels, chest up, depth to parallel or below. Control descent, explosive concentric. Focus on form over load.

items.name: Bent Over Row
items.cues: Hinge at hips with slight knee bend, neutral spine. Pull elbows high, squeeze shoulder blades together at top.

items.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
items.cues: Front knee tracks over ankle, rear leg elevated on bench. Descend controlled, front knee should not cave inward.

items.name: Cable Woodchop
items.cues: Rotate from core, keep arms relatively straight. Control the movement both directions. Engage obliques throughout.

items.name: Calf Stretch
items.cues: Keep heel planted, lean forward feeling stretch in calf. Hold each side 1 minute, breathe deeply.

items.name: Adductor Rockbacks
items.cues: Rock body weight back gently, feel inner thigh stretch. Move smoothly and hold stretch at deepest point.

items.name: Biceps Wall Stretch
items.cues: Arm extended at shoulder height against wall, rotate body away. Hold 1 minute each side.

rationale: With 6 days until the Engelbrektsloppet 45km race, this strength session builds lower body resilience and core stability critical for ultra-distance ski racing, focusing on compound movements that develop functional power.
Returning after 15 days of rest, this workout re-establishes strength foundations with RPE 6-7 intensity—challenging but controlled—allowing proper neural adaptation before peak training resumes.

Exercise selection emphasizes squat patterns, hip stability, and rotational core strength essential for maintaining form and power transfer throughout a 45km race while respecting recovery needs before race week.
